regions.label: Berlin
regions.note: Berlin charges 7.5% of the net room rate. The old 21-night cap was removed from 1 January 2025, so a normal stay is taxable throughout.

regions.label: Munich
regions.note: Munich charges no bed tax. Bavaria banned local hotel taxes, and the Bavarian Constitutional Court upheld that ban in 2025, so the city cannot levy one.

regions.label: Hamburg
regions.note: Hamburg uses a sliding scale by room price rather than a flat percentage; this is roughly equivalent to about 2% of the room rate.

regions.label: Cologne
regions.note: Cologne's culture tax (Kulturförderabgabe) runs 5% of the net room rate.

regions.label: Frankfurt
regions.note: Frankfurt charges a flat 2 euros per person, per night, rather than a percentage.

regions.label: Elsewhere in Germany
regions.note: Most German towns and smaller cities charge no bed tax at all. A separate Kurtaxe applies in officially designated spa and resort towns, typically 1.50 to 4 euros per person per night.
